parts: Lesson 25: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter — Summary
When light of suitable frequency falls on a metal, electrons are emitted (photoelectrons).

Observations: (1) there is a threshold frequency ν₀ below which no emission occurs, however intense the light; (2) the photocurrent (number of electrons) is proportional to the intensity — a straight line through the origin; (3) the maximum kinetic energy of the electrons depends on the frequency, not the intensity; (4) emission is instantaneous.

Stopping potential V₀ is the negative anode potential that just stops the fastest electrons: eV₀ = KE_max. For a given frequency it is the same for all intensities, while the saturation current grows with intensity.

Einstein's equation: light is made of photons of energy hν. KE_max = hν − φ, where the work function φ = hν₀. Examples: 5 eV photons on a metal with φ = 2.3 eV give KE_max = 2.7 eV; ν₀ = 5.6 × 10¹⁴ Hz gives φ = hν₀ ≈ 3.7 × 10⁻¹⁹ J (2.3 eV).
A graph of V₀ against ν is a straight line with slope h/e, cutting the ν-axis at ν₀.
X-rays, with high photon energy, cause photoemission far more readily than microwaves.
A photon has energy E = hν = hc/λ, momentum p = h/λ = hν/c, and moving (effective) mass m = E/c² = hν/c² = h/λc. It has zero rest mass.
Example: a 9 eV photon has p = 4.8 × 10⁻²⁷ kg m/s, and a hydrogen atom (1.6 × 10⁻²⁷ kg) emitting it recoils at 3 m/s.
Photocells change light into electric current. They are used in automatic doors and street lights, burglar alarms, light meters, sound reproduction from film, and solar power.
Moving particles have an associated wave of wavelength λ = h/p = h/mv.
For a charge q accelerated through V: λ = h/√(2mqV). For an electron, λ = 12.27/√V Å, so a graph of λ against √V is a rectangular hyperbola.
Equal momenta give equal λ (electron, proton or α). Equal kinetic energies give λ ∝ 1/√m, so λ_α < λ_p = λ_n < λ_e.
For α-particles and protons accelerated through the same p.d.: λ_α/λ_p = √(m_p q_p / m_α q_α) = 1/(2√2).
Matter waves were confirmed by the Davisson–Germer electron diffraction experiment.
